articles.body:
Atlético Madrid and Juventus are monitoring Arsenal winger Noni Madueke with a view to a loan move, while SC Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic has Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea on his trail. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Trending rumors

- Atlético Madrid and Juventus are monitoring Arsenal winger Noni Madueke with a view to a potential January loan move, according to The Telegraph. The 24-year-old has struggled for game time this season, logging just 23 minutes across two substitute Premier League appearances, as Bukayo Saka and new arrival Christos Tzolis have impressed in the wide berths.

- Manchester United are tracking SC Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic alongside Arsenal and Chelsea, TEAMtalk reports. The 23-year-old Croatia international has 21 goals in 57 games for the club and his transfer is valued at €60 million, with United keen to bolster up front amid Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury issues. Arsenal could move on Viktor Gyökeres, while Chelsea have identified him as a backup option to João Pedro.

- Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is closing in on a new contract through 2029 following a breakthrough in talks, according to Sky Deutschland. The 33-year-old, who has scored 152 goals and provided 34 assists in 154 matches for the club, is set to commit his future to the Allianz Arena despite previous links with Barcelona.

- Arsenal are exploring a move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, but Los Blancos will only entertain a straight loan without permanent option clauses in January, TEAMtalk reports. The 20-year-old Brazil international, who has also been linked with Roma, remains highly regarded by the Spanish club despite his frustration over a lack of minutes.

- AC Milan are planning a January approach for Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, per Calciomercato. The Rossoneri hope to agree an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for the 25-year-old to complete an attacking line featuring Gonçalo Ramos and Francesco Camarda.

- Real Madrid attacking midfielder Arda Güler has agreed a two-year contract extension until 2031 with an improved salary. (Diario AS)

- AC Milan have internally discussed a free transfer for 34-year-old former Real Madrid right back Dani Carvajal, following an injury to Pervis Estupiñán. (Calciomercato)

- Liverpool plan to reject loan or permanent interest in defender Giovanni Leoni from Juventus and Internazionale. (Football Insider)

- Manchester United, Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea and Manchester City are all keeping tabs on Barcelona right back Jules Koundé. (SPORT)

articles.headline: Fantasy football consistency ratings: 2024 to 2026
articles.description: The consistency ratings weigh both how consistent and how start-worthy players have been from 2024 to 2026.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジーフットボール安定度評価：2024年〜2026年
articles.descriptionJa: この安定度評価では、2024年から2026年にかけて、選手がいかに安定しており、またいかに先発起用に見合う活躍をしたかを測定しています。
articles.body:
Updated Oct. 6, 2026 (through Week 4 of 2026)

How consistency ratings work

Using fantasy points determined by ESPN's standard scoring, the charts contained in this column rate players based upon how consistently reliable they have been during the 2024 through 2026 seasons, a span of 40 weeks' worth of games (18 weeks apiece in 2024 and 2025, four so far in 2026). For IDPs (individual defensive players), the scoring from our weekly rankings is used: solo tackle (1.5), assisted tackle (0.75), tackle for loss (2), sack (4), interception (5), forced fumble (4), fumble recovery (4), touchdown (6), safety (2), pass defended (1.5). To familiarize you with the terminology and column headers listed in the charts below:

Start%: The player's "start percentage," which shows how often he earned a start in an ESPN standard PPR (points per reception) league. This is his number of "starts" -- those defined below -- divided by his number of scheduled team games.

CR: The player's "consistency rating," which is calculated as his weekly standard deviation divided by his PPR fantasy points per game average. This is meant to identify the players who were most consistently close to their weekly averages. The lower the number, the more consistent the player. Again, lower numbers are better.

nPPR%: The player's start percentage using non-PPR scoring, using ESPN's standard scoring settings without any points per reception.

FPTS/G: The player's average PPR fantasy points scored per game.

Start: The number of times that the player's point total in a given week was worthy of having had him active in an ESPN standard PPR league.

Star: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the best at his position.

Stiff: The number of times the player's point total ranked among the worst at his position, making almost any waiver-wire option a smarter choice.

These are the benchmarks for what constitutes a "start," "star" or "stiff" performance:

Sat: The number of times the player sat out a game. Players are not charged "stiff" points for sitting out, nor does it impact their overall consistency rating (CR), but it hurts their overall start percentage.

Players must have a start rate of at least 20% in either standard PPR or non-PPR scoring, rank among the top 20 quarterbacks, tight ends or kickers, top 50 running backs or wide receivers, or top 40 defensive linemen, linebackers or defensive backs, in terms of total fantasy points at their position from 2024 to 2026, or are averaging at least 50 snaps per game, for inclusion in the chart. All defense/special teams are included regardless of whether they meet those minimums.

articles.headline: Eagles All-Pro RT Lane Johnson retires, ending 14-season NFL career
articles.description: Eagles two-time All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement Tuesday, ending a 14-year career spent entirely in Philadelphia.
articles.headlineJa: イーグルスのオールプロRTレーン・ジョンソンが引退、14シーズンのNFLキャリアに幕
articles.descriptionJa: イーグルスで2度のオールプロ選出を誇るライトタックルのレーン・ジョンソンが火曜日に引退を表明し、フィラデルフィアのみで過ごした14年間のキャリアに終止符を打った。
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles two-time All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson announced his retirement Tuesday, ending a 14-year career spent entirely in Philadelphia.

Johnson, 36, who is considered one of the top offensive tackles in the NFL, was a surprise inactive on Sunday with the Eagles saying it was for personal reasons.

"I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season. But after a lot of reflection, I've realized that my personal and family priorities have changed. Right now it is critical that I focus on my mental health," he wrote in a statement posted to social media.

"I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game. And right now my heart is telling me that it's time to say goodbye to football."

A two-time Super Bowl champion, Johnson has made the Pro Bowl six times in his career.

Oct. 6

Doncic, who 'worked his butt off all summer,' lights up Kings

A lighter Luka Doncic scored an easy 21 first-half points in the Los Angeles Lakers' preseason opener over the Sacramento Kings on Monday night, needing only 16 minutes to sharpen up his game in a 127-103 blowout in Sacramento.
Doncic was listed at 244 pounds prior to the 2025-26 season. That dipped to 230 pounds entering training camp. The difference in physique from his heavier days is obvious.

"The guy worked his butt off all summer staying in shape and actually ran this summer," coach JJ Redick said. "He actually did like sprints and stuff. Came into camp in fantastic shape."

The Lakers were without Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler in the preseason opener. Reaves tweaked his ankle recently, and Kessler jammed a finger on the backboard. Both are listed as day-to-day. Without either, the Lakers still rolled through the Kings. Doncic scored all 21 of his points in a 73-point Lakers first half, resting while the backups finished the job. He made three 3s, four shots in the paint and got to the line for nine free throws.

"For someone who normally plays a ton of live basketball [in the summer], he didn't do as much of that by design," Redick said. "We've seen him literally every day in camp incrementally get more and more in rhythm."

Doncic badly strained his hamstring in early April and missed the entire Lakers playoff run while rehabbing the injury. He said he felt "great" against the Kings but downplayed any larger changes to his training regimen.

"I feel probably a little more rested," Doncic said. "I didn't play [on the Slovenian] national team." -- Anthony Slater

articles.headline: Portugal, Man United, Real Madrid: Cristiano Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches
articles.description: Cristiano Ronaldo walked out of the Portugal national team's camp after being benched. It is far from the first high-profile row of his two decades at the top.
articles.headlineJa: ポルトガル、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、レアル・マドリード：クリスティアーノ・ロナウドと監督たちの長く続く不仲の歴史
articles.descriptionJa: クリスティアーノ・ロナウドはベンチ外となった後、ポルトガル代表キャンプを離脱した。トップレベルで活躍した20年間において、こうした世間の注目を集める衝突は決して初めてのことではない。
articles.body:
Editor's note: This has been updated after Cristiano Ronaldo released a statement on the events that led to his departure from Portugal's team camp.

Was it always going to end like this? Cristiano Ronaldo -- Portugal's greatest-ever player, who led them to victory at the 2016 UEFA European Championship, and won the UEFA Champions League and the Ballon d'Or five times in a glittering club career -- walked away from the national team's camp on Wednesday, leaving his international future in doubt.

Ronaldo, 41, has since then spoken about the reasons for his departure. Days earlier, coach Jorge Jesus had insisted there was "no issue," but admitted mistakes in his handling of Ronaldo's role in Sunday's 2-1 win over Norway in the UEFA Nations League, where he was an unused substitute.

It is still unclear whether his departure means he has played his last game for Portugal. However, sources tell ESPN that Ronaldo has issued an ultimatum that he will not return to the national team while Jesus is the coach. But an acrimonious end to his international career -- during which he has scored a men's record 146 goals -- could hardly be described as a shock.

- Ronaldo goal tracker: 978 and counting on road to 1,000 career goals

- A kit fit for the GOAT: Messi's special kit for final Argentina match

- LaLiga unveils Clásico match ball for Barça vs. Real Madrid clashes

Managing the transition when an aging superstar's performance level drops is never easy, and Ronaldo's role and impact -- positive and negative -- with Portugal has been debated for three successive major tournaments now, in 2022, 2024 and 2026.

Throughout his 25-year career, Ronaldo has been involved in a series of headline-grabbing disagreements with managers, teammates and executives. As we wait for this latest drama to be resolved, here are some of the most high-profile previous examples.

Unhappy Ronaldo backs Blatter's insensitive "slavery" comparison (July 10, 2008)

Ronaldo's bid to leave Manchester United for Real Madrid that summer reached a new, histrionic high -- or low -- when Ronaldo echoed comments from then-FIFA president Sepp Blatter that keeping a player at a club against their will was comparable to "modern slavery." Ronaldo told Portugal's TV1: "It's true. I agree with what the president of FIFA said. I know what I want and what I would like. We have to see what happens. I do not know where I will begin next season." After five successful years at Old Trafford, Ronaldo was ready to move on, but United stood firm and the forward had to wait another season before his desired move to the Bernabéu was finally fulfilled.

articles.headline: Three of Nolan Wells' friends sue Terrell Owens for defamation
articles.description: Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Black college student who went missing from a Mississippi island during a Fourth of July celebration and was later found dead, are suing Terrell Owens for defamation.
articles.headlineJa: ノーラン・ウェルズの友人3人がテレル・オーウェンスを名誉毀損で提訴
articles.descriptionJa: 独立記念日の祝祭中にミシシッピ島の島から行方不明となり、後に遺体で発見された黒人の大学生、ノーラン・ウェルズの友人3人が、テレル・オーウェンスを名誉毀損で提訴している。
articles.body:
JACKSON, Miss. -- Three friends of Nolan Wells, a Black college student who went missing from a Mississippi island during a Fourth of July celebration and was later found dead, are suing Pro Football Hall of Famer Terrell Owens for defamation.

Lawyers for the friends said they intend to file several more defamation claims this week against content creators and have previously indicated their intent to sue the Rev. Al Sharpton and "The View" co-host Sunny Hostin for comments they made while discussing Wells' death.

The fathers of the three friends, who are under 21 and considered minors under Mississippi law, filed the federal lawsuit Monday on their behalf.

The lawsuit alleges Owens defamed the three friends after posting on X: "ARREST THEM IMMEDIATELY!!" Owens' post also linked to an Instagram video, which theorized the three friends killed Wells and tampered with his phone, according to the lawsuit. The post was made days after a Mississippi grand jury declined to recommend charges in Wells' death.

Owens has 1.2 million followers on X and had previously pledged $25,000 to a reward fund for information leading to an arrest and conviction in Wells' death.

"Not only is he defaming them, he's basically saying to the mob, get your pitchforks, get your torches," said Edward Paltzik, a defamation and media attorney representing the three friends.

The Associated Press attempted to contact Owens through social media and SMAC Entertainment, which, according to its website, manages Owens, but did not immediately receive a response.

The three were part of a group of 30 friends, including Wells, who rode to Horn Island on three boats on the Fourth of July. Wells' friends said Wells did not return to the mainland with them, choosing instead to stay behind to talk with a girl, a claim his family has disputed. His body was found two days later off the island's coast.

Both state and independent autopsies have not determined Wells' cause of death, though the grand jury found his death was "consistent with drowning." Wells' family and their lawyers disputed the grand jury's findings, pointing to unexplained bruising on the back of his head and noting that his airways and stomach were devoid of water.

Images showing Wells with white friends the day he went missing fueled online speculation that racial dynamics played a role in his death.

Two of the three friends who are suing Owens were singled out online in part because they appear in a photo with Wells and one other friend on a boat, which was circulated on social media after his disappearance. The third called Wells' mother and the U.S. Coast Guard to report Wells missing.

articles.headline: 76ers lose backup center Ariel Hukporti to torn Achilles
articles.description: The 76ers' thin frontcourt took a big blow Tuesday after an MRI confirmed backup center Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn right Achilles.
articles.headlineJa: 76ers、控えセンターのアリエル・ハクポーティがアキレス腱断裂で離脱
articles.descriptionJa: 火曜日のMRI検査によって控えセンターのアリエル・ハクポーティの右アキレス腱断裂が確認され、層の薄い76ersのフロントコートにとって大きな痛手となった。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- An MRI confirmed Tuesday that Philadelphia 76ers center Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn right Achilles tendon in the Sixers preseason opener Monday, the team announced.

Hukporti will undergo surgery Tuesday, according to the team, and further updates will be provided as appropriate

The 24-year-old big man out of Germany signed to a one-year, $3.4 million free agent contract with Philadelphia in July after winning a championship with the New York Knicks.

 

The Sixers are eligible to apply for and get awarded a $1.7 million Disabled Player Exception (half of Hukporti's 2026-27 salary), according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

However, with Philadelphia only $1.8 million below the first apron, they cannot sign a player to replace Hukporti to their open roster spot without either waiving a player or making a small trade to free up more cap space.

Philadelphia does have an open two-way spot it can look to fill with a center also. The Sixers signed 7-foot-5 big man Tacko Fall to an Exhibit 10 training camp deal as a chance to audition for the two-way spot, but Fall is currently sidelined with a left hip strain and will be reevaluated in approximately 7-10 days, according to the team.

The Sixers are also without the last remaining center on the roster, Adem Bona, who has yet to participate in training camp due to a left foot sprain. However, the team hopes he will be available at some point during preseason.

Including start Joel Embiid, the Sixers' other frontcourt options are Dean Wade, Dominick Barlow and Jabari Walker.

Philadelphia's regular-season opener is Oct. 20 in New York against the Knicks.

articles.descriptionJa: ジム・マコーミックが、新しいファンタジーバスケットボールシーズンに向けて、あらゆる変更点と知っておくべきポイントを解説します。
articles.body:
Maybe your fantasy football team has started the season like the Los Angeles Chargers. In fact, maybe your fantasy football team is full of Los Angeles Chargers. Either way, welcome to another season of fantasy hoops.

Whether making an annual gridiron-to-hardwood pivot or coming to our game for the first time, you need not track every Shams Charania post or dissect every roster to get up to speed. We have you covered.

Some blend of the second apron -- think Jaylen Brown -- and second destinations -- Ja Morant and LaMelo Ball -- drove many of this summer's biggest moves. The goal is to decipher meaningful changes in the fantasy basketball landscape after a busy, dramatic offseason.

The All-Star Carousel

You know the big names who changed teams, but who is set to surge or sacrifice statistically? With apologies to Khris Middleton and D'Angelo Russell, we'll conduct a stock report on the following former All-Stars who changed teams this offseason. To get a sense of how the market values them, they are listed in order of ESPN average draft position.

Familiar First-rounder: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Miami Heat

A lost final season in Milwaukee gives way to a featured role in a coaching culture that gets the most out of elite, versatile forwards. Will the Heat lead the league in pace again now that this pick-and-roll engine is rostered? If the tempo remains, could this be his best statistical season in years? Consider me, along with Pat Riley, a believer

Health Permitting: LaMelo Ball, Minnesota Timberwolves and Kawhi Leonard, Toronto Raptors

Ball will almost certainly average more than the modest 28 minutes per game he hovered around in Charlotte last year. The front office consolidated the rotation, putting this big, brilliant playmaker on track for 30-plus minutes per night. Charlotte's breakneck, shoot-first system was ideal for his skill set, leaving a real question of offensive fit. Fit and health make Ball a risky, potentially rewarding pick.

Leonard is also in a better position to produce in Toronto; Scottie Barnes can take the toughest, most physical defensive assignments while providing playmaking gravity. Leonard is a league-winner if he plays more than 65 games.

Which Philly Forward? Jaylen Brown and LeBron James

This one is simple: Brown's potential to repeat last season's epic, MVP-caliber campaign is, well, quite low. Even with the market pricing in an expected sacrifice, it's hard to envision Brown providing a fantasy profit. Despite my Philly fandom, it's sensible to fade Brown.

James, on the other hand, could outperform his draft spot in a table-setting role rich in potential-and realized-assists. With pocket passes to Joel Embiid and slashes from Brown, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe, can James recapture, or at least approach, the playmaking form that carried him to the passing title as the point guard of the 2019-20 Lakers?

What happens next? What does the ruling mean for England's dominant force over the past decade, its fans and its players? ESPN's writers have you covered on every angle, from transfer implications to the mood at City's rival clubs.

Check back here for the latest as this story continues to unfold.

articles.headline: Predicting how new NBA lottery, anti-tanking rules will impact 2026-27 season
articles.description: How could the changes aimed at circumventing tanking likely affect on-court outcomes this season?
articles.headlineJa: NBAの新しいロタリーおよびアンチタンキング規則が2026-27シーズンに与える影響を予想
articles.descriptionJa: タンキング（意図的な弱体化）を回避するためのルール変更が、今シーズンのコート上の結果にどのような影響を与える可能性があるのか。
articles.body:
This NBA season, for the first time, teams can't win by losing. After a tanktastic 2025-26 campaign, the league has instituted a new draft lottery setup with several new features, including:

Flat lottery odds for the teams with the fourth- through 10th-worst records

A "relegation zone" in which the three worst teams get worse odds of landing a top pick

A lottery that draws each of the first 16 picks, rather than just the first four from the old system

This new setup will invariably produce plenty of ripple effects as teams respond to new incentives with new behaviors. Exactly how much things will change, and how these anti-tanking measures might alter transactional decisions such as the trade and buyout markets, remains to be seen.

But for now, here are five predictions for how the new rules will affect on-court outcomes in the 2026-27 season.

Fewer blowouts

In the 2025-26 regular season, 281 games were decided by at least 20 points, which broke the record of 259 set just one year earlier ... which broke the record of 235 set just one year before that ... which broke the record of 232 set just two years before that.

On a percentage basis, last season set a record, too. On a percentage basis, last season set a record, too, as 22% of games were blowouts. If you rank every season in NBA history by the proportion of games decided by 20-plus points, five of the top six have come since 2021.

While the leaguewide blowout rate remained relatively consistent through the first 70-plus years of NBA history, it has skyrocketed in the 2020s.

Several factors explain this sudden rise, including the increased variance of 3-pointers and a general rise in offense; it's easier to win by 20 points when the average team scores 115 points per game instead of 95. But when scoring was also high in the 1960s and 1980s, blowout rates in those decades weren't close to where they are now.

Instead, it appears that teams' modern approach to late-season games has skewed competitiveness. The NBA's blowout rate increased considerably as the 2025-26 season went on, especially in games involving tanking teams. From the start of February through the end of the season, a full third of games involving the NBA's worst teams ended with at least a 20-point margin.

Now that the league's cellar-dwellers no longer have an incentive to keep losing -- and in fact might have an incentive to win games to avoid the relegation zone -- the blowout rate should theoretically stop spiking in February, March and April.

Broader increases in competitiveness could also make the league's best teams look a little less dominant. In the 2024-25 season, when the Thunder set an NBA record with a plus-12.9 point differential, they received a big boost from competition that wasn't trying to win. articles.headline: Viktor Gyökeres to make Arsenal return after goal-laden stint with Sweden
articles.description: Viktor Gyökeres will return to Arsenal in confident mood after setting a new Nations League record with four more goals for Sweden over the international break.
articles.headlineJa: ヴィクトル・ギョケレス、スウェーデン代表でのゴール量産を経てアーセナルに復帰へ
articles.descriptionJa: 代表ウィーク中にスウェーデン代表としてさらに4ゴールを決め、ネーションズリーグの新たな記録を樹立したヴィクトル・ギョケレスは、自信に満ちた状態でアーセナルへ復帰します。
articles.body:
Viktor Gyökeres will return to Arsenal in confident mood after setting a new Nations League record with four goals in four games for Sweden over the international break.

Gyökeres was on target to give Sweden a 1-0 win over Romania in Bucharest on Monday night, extending his scoring streak in the competition to seven straight games.

The 28-year-old, who signed for Arsenal from Sporting Lisbon in a £64 million ($85m) deal last summer, has been used sparingly so far this season by Gunners boss Mikel Arteta, making just two substitute appearances in the Premier League.

Gyökeres, though, showed few signs of a drop in confidence over the extended international window with goals in each of the fixtures, which started with a wins over Romania and Poland in Stockholm before a 1-1 draw away to Bosnia and Herzegovina as Sweden went top of Group B4.

With Germany forward Kai Havertz picking up a hamstring issue early in the break and returning to Arsenal for further assessment, Gyokeres could be brought back in to lead the Gunners' attack when Premier League action resumes against Leeds on Saturday.

"That [the goals for Sweden] means we win three games and draw one. It is a good start to the Nations League this year and for me it feels very good," Gyökeres told reporters, as quoted by SVT Sport.

"They [Romania] had the ball a bit too much and we made it difficult for ourselves at times, but we won the match and keep a clean sheet, so after the match it is a nice feeling."

Arsenal defender Riccardo Calafiori got his first goal for Italy in their 3-1 win over Turkey in Bologna.

Calafiori, who scored for Arsenal after only 24 seconds in the Community Shield win over Manchester City, is hoping to continue to make plenty of contributions in the opposition box.

"Last year, I was unlucky and I was close to at least five or six goals. This year the season started quite well, but obviously, beyond the numbers, I am interested in the contribution I give to the team," Calafiori said in an interview with Rai Sport.

"I try to be well physically -- in the end that is what matters, because when I am okay I can help in so many ways."

Versatile full-back Calafiori revealed Arteta has encouraged him to make the most of his attacking instincts.

"I spoke to the coach and he himself told me that if I have this impulse to go and attack the spaces I have to do it, because it comes naturally to me," he said.

articles.headline: Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season
articles.description: It's only October, but Real Madrid already face a potentially season-defining run of five games that ends with El Clásico. What does José Mourinho need to get right?
articles.headlineJa: ムリーニョ、レアル・マドリードのシーズンを救うための課題は山積み
articles.descriptionJa: まだ10月に過ぎないが、レアル・マドリードはシーズンの運命を左右しかねない5試合の連続戦に直面している。その最後にはエル・クラシコが控えている。ジョゼ・ムリーニョに求められる正解とは何か？
articles.body:
At least Kylian Mbappé is laughing.

LaLiga is back this week, and the prognosis is already looking bleak for Real Madrid. After seven games, they trail leaders Barcelona by six points, with a high-stakes Clásico to come at Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barça's record so far is played seven, won seven. They've got a +24 goal difference, they've got Lamine Yamal, and they've got Raphinha in career-best form. From a Madrid point of view, this could get ugly.

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

But Mbappé looked carefree enough on Sunday as he posted a self-recorded video on social media, smiling while riding a bike in what looked like an idyllic country setting.

There was just one problem: his manager José Mourinho had mentioned cycling in an interview 10 days earlier, citing it as a specific example of the kind of hobbies footballers must not undertake, given their responsibilities.

"You cannot ride a bike," Mourinho said, categorically. "You fall off, and maybe you don't play three matches, or maybe worse, you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player."

Was Mbappé unaware of Mourinho's comments? Was this just an unfortunate coincidence? Or was there some other, as-yet unknown intent behind Mbappé's post, a message being sent? We'll hear Mourinho's response on Friday, as he speaks to the media the day before Madrid's game with Villarreal at the Bernabéu (stream LIVE 10/10 at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

In the meantime, Mbappé's off-field activities might not even rank among Mourinho's biggest worries this week as he works with his players on the training pitches at Valdebebas.

Mourinho has only been back at Madrid for three months. Now he has a run of five games -- Villarreal (home) on Saturday, AS Roma (away) on Oct. 14, Sevilla (home) on Oct. 18, RB Leipzig (home) on Oct. 21 and then Barcelona (away) four days later -- to get Madrid's season back on track, or risk derailing his project entirely.

So, what's the Real Madrid's to-do list ahead such a potentially season-defining set of fixtures?

Find Vinícius Júnior's best form

In eight Real Madrid games this season, Vinícius Júnior has scored just one goal, a close-range tap-in against Real Sociedad on Aug. 26. And when you look at the numbers, it gets even worse.

Take his personal, expected goal tallies against Espanyol (0.04 in 90 minutes), Málaga (0.04 in 90 minutes), Inter Milan (0.1 in 87 minutes), Rayo Vallecano (0.15 in 89 minutes) and Atlético Madrid (0.06 in 54 minutes).

Vinícius hasn't been scoring goals; he hasn't even looked like scoring goals. He's struggled to get into dangerous positions, and he's failed to convert on the rare occasions that he has.

articles.headline: Liverpool sweating over Jeremy Jacquet fitness ahead of Man City clash
articles.description: Liverpool are waiting to discover the extent of Jeremy Jacquet's fitness issue after the centre-back was left out of France's Nations League win over Belgium.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティ戦を前に、リヴァプールはジェレミー・ジャケのコンディションを懸念
articles.descriptionJa: フランスのネーションズリーグにおけるベルギー戦にこのセンターバックが選出されなかったことを受け、リヴァプールはジェレミー・ジャケのコンディション不良がどの程度深刻なのかを見極めようとしている。
articles.body:
Liverpool are waiting to discover the extent of Jeremy Jacquet's fitness issue after the centre-back was left out of France's Nations League win over Belgium.

The defender had played the previous two matches, his first for the senior team, but was omitted from Zinedine Zidane's squad for Monday's 4-1 victory.

A statement from the French Football Federation said the 21-year-old had sustained a "strain to his left hamstring," while in his post-match press conference Zidane said Jacquet was "slightly injured."

Jacquet has featured in all seven matches for Liverpool this season, starting six alongside Virgil van Dijk in central defence.

Head coach Andoni Iraola has cover in the form of on-loan Barcelona defender Ronald Araújo and Joe Gomez, but Jacquet's potential absence for Sunday's visit of Manchester City would be a significant blow.

The Reds already have doubts over forwards Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, whose international exploits with Sweden and the Netherlands respectively were cut short.

Isak was sent home after just one match due to a minor thigh problem, with Gakpo more of a concern after injuring his ankle.

Summer signing Bradley Barcola could be pressed into action in a central role, even though he is more comfortable out wide, while Florian Wirtz could be moved further forward from his number 10 position.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.
